12|A0|First statement|subject + être + place|Keep the subject before the conjugated verb in an ordinary statement.|Je suis ici.|I am here.|Use suis with je, not est.|subject:Je^verb:suis^place:ici.

16|A1|Nationality and agreement|subject + être + adjective|A nationality used as an adjective is lowercase and agrees with the subject.|Elle est française.|She is French.|Write française for a feminine subject.|subject:Elle^verb:est^attribute:française.

50|A1|Having something|subject + avoir + noun phrase|Avoir expresses possession; include a determiner with a singular count noun.|J’ai un frère.|I have a brother.|Do not omit un before frère in this sentence.|subject and verb:J’ai^object:un frère.

55|A1|Age with avoir|subject + avoir + number + ans|French uses avoir for age.|J’ai trente ans.|I am thirty years old.|Do not translate English am with suis for age.|subject and verb:J’ai^age:trente ans.

22|A1|Identifying someone|c’est + noun phrase|Use c’est with a determiner and a noun to identify someone or something.|C’est mon voisin.|He is my neighbour.|Il est voisin and c’est mon voisin have different structures.|identification:C’est^noun phrase:mon voisin.

44|A1|Saying something exists|il y a + noun phrase + place|Il y a introduces existence; il is impersonal here.|Il y a une pharmacie ici.|There is a pharmacy here.|Do not change il to ils for plural objects.|existence:Il y a^noun phrase:une pharmacie^place:ici.

23|A1|Article and noun|article + noun|The article carries grammatical gender and number.|Le livre est ici.|The book is here.|Use le livre, not la livre, for a book.|subject noun phrase:Le livre^verb:est^place:ici.

26|A1|Elision|l’ + vowel or mute-h noun|Le and la become l’ before a vowel or mute h. An aspirated h blocks elision.|L’école est ouverte.|The school is open.|An apostrophe joins l’ to the next word.|subject noun phrase:L’école^verb:est^attribute:ouverte.

57|A1|Adjective agreement|noun + être + agreeing adjective|An adjective describing a feminine noun normally takes a feminine form.|La maison est petite.|The house is small.|Petite agrees with maison, not with the speaker.|subject:La maison^verb:est^attribute:petite.

59|A1|Common adjective before a noun|determiner + common adjective + noun|Many frequent adjectives such as petit, grand, beau and bon often precede a noun; meaning can affect position.|C’est un petit jardin.|It is a small garden.|Do not move every adjective before the noun.|identification:C’est^noun phrase:un petit jardin.

60|A1|Colour after the noun|determiner + noun + colour|Ordinary colour adjectives usually follow the noun.|Elle porte une veste bleue.|She is wearing a blue jacket.|Bleue agrees with veste; compound colour names have separate rules.|subject:Elle^verb:porte^object:une veste bleue.

58|A1|Plural agreement|plural determiner + plural noun + plural adjective|The determiner, noun and adjective show plural agreement in writing.|Les maisons sont petites.|The houses are small.|Most final plural s letters are silent.|subject:Les maisons^verb:sont^attribute:petites.

29|A1|Regular present statement|subject + conjugated verb + complement|Choose the finite ending for the subject. An ordinary statement needs a finite verb.|Nous parlons français.|We speak French.|Parlons is finite; parler is an infinitive.|subject:Nous^verb:parlons^complement:français.

89|A2|Modal and infinitive|subject + pouvoir/devoir/vouloir + infinitive|Only the first verb is conjugated when a modal directly governs an infinitive.|Je peux venir demain.|I can come tomorrow.|Use venir after peux, not viens.|subject:Je^modal:peux^infinitive:venir^time:demain.

160|B1|Action in progress|subject + être en train de + infinitive|This structure emphasizes an action happening now; the simple present is often sufficient.|Elle est en train de travailler.|She is in the middle of working.|Do not conjugate travailler after de.|subject:Elle^aspect phrase:est en train de^infinitive:travailler.

78|A1|Present negation|subject + ne + finite verb + pas|In standard written French, ne and pas surround the finite verb.|Je ne parle pas anglais.|I do not speak English.|Informal speech often drops ne; standard writing keeps it.|subject:Je^negation opening:ne^verb:parle^negation closing:pas^complement:anglais.

79|A1|Negation and a vowel|subject + n’ + vowel-initial finite verb + pas|Ne becomes n’ before a vowel or mute h.|Je n’aime pas ce film.|I do not like this film.|Use n’aime, not ne aime.|subject:Je^negated verb opening:n’aime^negation closing:pas^object:ce film.

80|A1|Never|subject + ne + finite verb + jamais|Jamais replaces pas when the meaning is never.|Elle ne fume jamais.|She never smokes.|Do not add pas to this ordinary jamais construction.|subject:Elle^negation opening:ne^verb:fume^frequency negation:jamais.

81|A1|No longer|subject + ne + finite verb + plus|Ne…plus means no longer; pronunciation differs from some affirmative uses of plus.|Nous ne travaillons plus ici.|We no longer work here.|Do not confuse ne…plus with more in a comparison.|subject:Nous^negation opening:ne^verb:travaillons^negation closing:plus^place:ici.

82|A1|Negative quantity|subject + ne + verb + pas de + noun|In an ordinary total negation, un, une, des and partitives often become de; être and contrasts have exceptions.|Je n’ai pas de voiture.|I do not have a car.|Ce n’est pas une voiture keeps une after être.|subject:Je^negative verb:n’ai pas^object:de voiture.

13|A0|Question with intonation|statement order + rising intonation|Keep the statement order and use question intonation in speech.|Tu es ici ?|Are you here?|A question mark alone does not change the written word order.|subject:Tu^verb:es^place:ici ?

40|A1|Question with est-ce que|est-ce que + subject + verb|Est-ce que introduces a neutral yes-or-no question.|Est-ce que tu comprends ?|Do you understand?|Do not also invert tu and comprends in this construction.|question marker:Est-ce que^subject:tu^verb:comprends ?

38|A1|Question word|question word + est-ce que + subject + verb|Place a question word before est-ce que to ask for a specific detail.|Où est-ce que vous habitez ?|Where do you live?|Où has an accent when it means where.|question word:Où^question marker:est-ce que^subject:vous^verb:habitez ?

39|A1|Inverted question|question word + verb-subject pronoun|Inversion is common in formal questions; join the finite verb and pronoun with a hyphen.|Quand partez-vous ?|When are you leaving?|The hyphen belongs between partez and vous.|question word:Quand^inverted verb and subject:partez-vous ?

41|A1|Which noun|quel/quelle/quels/quelles + noun|Quel agrees with the noun it introduces.|Quelle heure est-il ?|What time is it?|Heure is feminine singular, so use quelle.|question noun phrase:Quelle heure^inversion:est-il ?

53|A1|Possessive determiner|possessive determiner + possessed noun|The determiner agrees with the possessed noun. Mon, ton and son also precede a feminine singular noun beginning with a vowel or mute h.|Son amie arrive.|His or her friend is arriving.|Son does not tell you whether the possessor is male or female.|subject:Son amie^verb:arrive.

54|A1|Possession with de|possessed noun + de + possessor|Use de to name the possessor rather than an English apostrophe-s.|C’est le vélo de Léa.|It is Léa’s bicycle.|Do not add an English possessive s to Léa.|identification:C’est^possessed noun:le vélo^possessor:de Léa.

71|A1|Location|subject + être + place phrase|A prepositional phrase can locate a person or thing.|Le sac est sous la table.|The bag is under the table.|Choose the preposition for the actual spatial relationship.|subject:Le sac^verb:est^place:sous la table.

75|A1|À contractions|à + le = au; à + les = aux|À contracts with le and les; it does not contract with la or l’.|Je vais au marché.|I am going to the market.|Use au marché, not à le marché.|subject:Je^verb:vais^destination:au marché.

76|A1|De contractions|de + le = du; de + les = des|De contracts with le and les; it does not contract with la or l’.|Je reviens du marché.|I am coming back from the market.|Use du marché, not de le marché.|subject:Je^verb:reviens^origin:du marché.

72|A1|At someone’s place|chez + person or professional|Chez introduces a person’s home, workplace or professional premises.|Je vais chez mes amis.|I am going to my friends’ home.|Do not omit chez when this is the intended meaning.|subject:Je^verb:vais^destination:chez mes amis.

63|A1|Quantity with de|quantity expression + de/d’ + noun|After beaucoup, assez and similar quantity expressions, use de before the noun.|Nous avons beaucoup de temps.|We have a lot of time.|Use beaucoup de temps, not beaucoup du temps, for an unspecified quantity.|subject:Nous^verb:avons^quantity object:beaucoup de temps.

65|A1|Partitive article|du/de la/de l’ + mass noun|A partitive article expresses an unspecified amount of a substance.|Je bois de l’eau.|I am drinking water.|Do not replace de l’eau with des eau.|subject:Je^verb:bois^object:de l’eau.

113|A2|Near future|subject + aller in the present + infinitive|The present of aller introduces a planned or imminent action.|Nous allons partir demain.|We are going to leave tomorrow.|Only allons is conjugated; partir remains infinitive.|subject:Nous^auxiliary-like verb:allons^infinitive:partir^time:demain.

99|A2|Passé composé with avoir|subject + avoir in the present + past participle|The auxiliary carries person and tense; the participle carries the lexical action.|J’ai regardé un film.|I watched a film.|Use regardé, not regarder, after ai in this compound tense.|subject and auxiliary:J’ai^participle:regardé^object:un film.

100|A2|Passé composé with être|subject + être in the present + agreeing participle|A listed set of verbs and reflexive constructions use être. Agreement depends on the construction.|Elle est arrivée hier.|She arrived yesterday.|Arrivée agrees with elle in this ordinary être construction.|subject:Elle^auxiliary:est^participle:arrivée^time:hier.

103|A2|Compound negation|subject + ne + auxiliary + pas + participle|Place the main negation around the finite auxiliary, not around the participle.|Je n’ai pas compris.|I did not understand.|The order is n’ai pas compris, not ai compris pas.|subject:Je^negative auxiliary:n’ai pas^participle:compris.

106|A2|Past background|imperfect clause|The imperfect describes past states, background or repeated habits rather than marking every event as complete.|Il faisait froid.|It was cold.|The imperfect is not an English word-by-word translation rule.|subject:Il^verb:faisait^attribute:froid.

109|A2|Background and event|imperfect + quand + passé composé|An ongoing past activity can provide the background for a completed event.|Je lisais quand tu as appelé.|I was reading when you called.|Keep the two viewpoints distinct rather than using one tense mechanically.|background:Je lisais^connector:quand^event:tu as appelé.

114|A2|Simple future|subject + future form + time phrase|The simple future uses a finite future form, including irregular stems.|Nous partirons lundi.|We will leave on Monday.|Use partirons, not partiront, with nous.|subject:Nous^verb:partirons^time:lundi.

166|B1|Polite conditional|subject + conditional request|The conditional can soften a request or preference.|Je voudrais un café.|I would like a coffee.|Je veux is more direct than je voudrais.|subject:Je^verb:voudrais^object:un café.

175|B1|Real future condition|si + present, future|Use the present after si for a possible future condition; the result can be in the future.|Si tu viens, nous sortirons.|If you come, we will go out.|Do not use the future directly after conditional si here.|condition:Si tu viens,^result:nous sortirons.

176|B1|Hypothetical condition|si + imperfect, conditional present|Use the imperfect for an imagined condition and the conditional for its result.|Si j’avais le temps, je voyagerais.|If I had time, I would travel.|Do not use the conditional directly after this si.|condition:Si j’avais le temps,^result:je voyagerais.

182|B1|Desire and the subjunctive|wish clause + que + new subject + subjunctive|A wish concerning another subject commonly introduces the subjunctive.|Je veux que tu viennes.|I want you to come.|Use viennes after que in this construction, not viens.|wish:Je veux^connector:que^subject:tu^subjunctive: viennes.

183|B1|Necessity and the subjunctive|il faut que + subject + subjunctive|Il faut que introduces a finite subjunctive clause. Il faut + infinitive is another structure.|Il faut que nous partions.|We need to leave.|Use partions after il faut que.|necessity:Il faut^connector:que^subject:nous^subjunctive:partions.

120|A2|Direct object pronoun|subject + direct object pronoun + finite verb|Le, la and les usually precede an ordinary finite verb when they replace its direct object.|Je le vois.|I see him or it.|Voir takes a direct object; do not insert à.|subject:Je^object pronoun:le^verb:vois.

122|A2|Indirect object pronoun|subject + lui/leur + verb|Lui and leur can replace an à-person complement for verbs such as parler.|Je lui parle.|I am speaking to him or her.|Lui does not encode the person’s gender.|subject:Je^indirect object:lui^verb:parle.

247|B2|Two object pronouns|subject + le/la/les + lui/leur + finite verb|In this ordinary declarative combination, a direct object pronoun precedes lui or leur.|Je le lui donne.|I am giving it to him or her.|Affirmative imperatives use a different pronoun order.|subject:Je^direct object:le^indirect object:lui^verb:donne.

128|A2|Y for a place|subject + y + finite verb|Y can replace many place phrases introduced by à or another place preposition.|J’y vais demain.|I am going there tomorrow.|Do not repeat the place phrase unless you intend a special emphasis.|subject and pronoun:J’y^verb:vais^time:demain.

129|A2|En and quantity|subject + en + verb + retained quantity|En can replace a de-phrase; keep an expressed number or quantity.|J’en veux deux.|I want two of them.|The number remains after the verb.|subject and pronoun:J’en^verb:veux^quantity:deux.

92|A2|Reflexive routine|subject + reflexive pronoun + finite verb|The reflexive pronoun matches the subject; use elision when required.|Je me lève tôt.|I get up early.|Je lève and je me lève do not have the same construction.|subject:Je^reflexive pronoun:me^verb:lève^time:tôt.

104|A2|Reflexive past|subject + reflexive pronoun + être + participle|Reflexive compounds use être. Agreement must be checked against the reflexive pronoun’s grammatical function.|Elle s’est levée tôt.|She got up early.|Do not generalize this agreement to elle s’est lavé les mains.|subject:Elle^reflexive and auxiliary:s’est^participle:levée^time:tôt.

118|A2|Recent past|subject + venir de + infinitive|Venir de + infinitive expresses a recently completed event.|Je viens de finir.|I have just finished.|Finir remains an infinitive after de.|subject:Je^recent-past phrase:viens de^infinitive:finir.

140|A2|Comparative adjective|plus/moins/aussi + adjective + que|Use que to introduce the comparison target.|Ce trajet est plus court que l’autre.|This journey is shorter than the other one.|Use meilleur for better when comparing bon.|subject:Ce trajet^verb:est^comparison:plus court^comparison target:que l’autre.

141|A2|Superlative|definite article + plus/moins + adjective|A superlative identifies an extreme member within a group.|C’est le trajet le plus court.|It is the shortest journey.|Keep the definite article required by the chosen construction.|identification:C’est^noun phrase:le trajet^superlative:le plus court.

155|B1|Relative subject qui|noun + qui + finite verb|Qui acts as the subject inside this relative clause.|Je connais la personne qui arrive.|I know the person who is arriving.|Do not add another subject pronoun after qui.|main clause:Je connais la personne^relative subject:qui^relative verb:arrive.

156|B1|Relative object que|noun + que + subject + verb|Que represents a direct object inside this relative clause.|Voici le livre que tu cherches.|Here is the book you are looking for.|Chercher takes a direct object; que has that role here.|main clause:Voici le livre^relative object:que^relative subject:tu^relative verb:cherches.

157|B1|Relative place où|place noun + où + clause|Où can introduce a relative clause about a place or time.|C’est la ville où je travaille.|It is the city where I work.|Do not use ou without an accent for where.|main clause:C’est la ville^relative connector:où^relative clause:je travaille.

158|B1|Relative de-complement dont|noun + dont + clause|Dont can replace a complement introduced by de.|C’est le livre dont je parle.|It is the book I am talking about.|Do not repeat de after dont in this pattern.|main clause:C’est le livre^relative connector:dont^relative clause:je parle.

43|A1|Giving a reason|main clause + parce que + reason|Parce que connects a statement to its reason.|Je reste ici parce qu’il pleut.|I am staying here because it is raining.|Que elides before il.|main clause:Je reste ici^reason connector:parce qu’il^reason verb:pleut.

252|B2|Concession with bien que|bien que + subjunctive, main clause|Bien que introduces a concession and normally takes the subjunctive.|Bien qu’il soit tard, nous continuons.|Although it is late, we are continuing.|Use soit rather than est after bien que here.|concession:Bien qu’il soit tard,^main clause:nous continuons.

270|B2|Contrast with pourtant|clause; pourtant, contrasting clause|Pourtant marks an unexpected contrast between two assertions.|Il est fatigué ; pourtant, il continue.|He is tired; nevertheless, he continues.|Punctuation separates the two assertions in this model.|first clause:Il est fatigué ;^connector:pourtant,^contrast:il continue.

254|B2|Purpose with an infinitive|main clause + pour/afin de + infinitive|An infinitive purpose clause normally shares its understood subject with the main clause.|Je révise pour réussir l’examen.|I am reviewing to pass the exam.|Use pour que + a finite clause if a different subject must be expressed.|main clause:Je révise^purpose connector:pour^purpose:réussir l’examen.

253|B2|Before doing something|main clause + avant de + infinitive|Avant de introduces an infinitive with the same understood subject.|Je vérifie avant de répondre.|I check before answering.|Avant que introduces a finite subjunctive clause instead.|main clause:Je vérifie^time connector:avant de^infinitive:répondre.

239|B2|Earlier past with pluperfect|imperfect auxiliary + past participle|The pluperfect locates an event before another past reference point.|J’avais déjà mangé quand il est arrivé.|I had already eaten when he arrived.|Do not use a present auxiliary for the earlier past in this model.|earlier event:J’avais déjà mangé^connector:quand^later event:il est arrivé.

261|B2|Reported speech in the past|past reporting verb + que + shifted tense|An imperfect can report a state simultaneous with a past act of speaking.|Elle a dit qu’elle était prête.|She said that she was ready.|Tense choices depend on time relations and whether the statement remains current.|reporting clause:Elle a dit^reported clause:qu’elle était prête.

263|B2|Passive voice|patient subject + être + agreeing past participle|The passive makes the affected person or thing the grammatical subject.|La porte est fermée par le gardien.|The door is closed by the caretaker.|The passive participle agrees with porte.|subject:La porte^auxiliary:est^participle:fermée^agent:par le gardien.

248|B2|Gérondif|en + present participle|The gérondif often expresses simultaneous action or manner with the same subject.|Elle écoute en prenant des notes.|She listens while taking notes.|The understood subject of prenant is elle.|main clause:Elle écoute^gérondif:en prenant^object:des notes.

285|B2|Focusing the subject|c’est + focus + qui + verb|The cleft construction highlights the subject.|C’est Léa qui organise la réunion.|It is Léa who is organising the meeting.|Qui introduces the subject focus; que has other roles.|focus:C’est Léa^relative subject:qui^predicate:organise la réunion.

310|C1|Concession with a noun|en dépit de + noun phrase, clause|En dépit de introduces a noun phrase rather than a finite clause.|En dépit du retard, nous sommes arrivés à temps.|Despite the delay, we arrived on time.|De + le contracts to du.|concession:En dépit du retard,^main clause:nous sommes arrivés à temps.

311|C1|Even if|même si + indicative clause|Même si generally takes the indicative, unlike bien que.|Même si le résultat est imparfait, il reste utile.|Even if the result is imperfect, it remains useful.|Do not automatically use the subjunctive after même si.|concession:Même si le résultat est imparfait,^main clause:il reste utile.

312|C1|Condition with pourvu que|pourvu que + subjunctive|Pourvu que introduces a condition or a wish with the subjunctive.|Nous partirons pourvu qu’il fasse beau.|We will leave provided the weather is good.|Use fasse after pourvu que.|main clause:Nous partirons^condition:pourvu qu’il fasse beau.

366|C2|Formal hypothetical concession|quand bien même + conditional, conditional result|Quand bien même introduces a hypothetical concession in a formal register.|Quand bien même il refuserait, nous continuerions.|Even if he refused, we would continue.|This formal construction differs from the ordinary même s’il refusait model.|hypothesis:Quand bien même il refuserait,^result:nous continuerions.

330|C1|Source comparison|source attribution + tandis que + contrasting source|Explicitly attribute claims when contrasting sources in a synthesis.|Le premier texte insiste sur le coût, tandis que le second souligne les avantages.|The first text stresses the cost, while the second highlights the benefits.|Do not present a source’s claim as your own unsupported fact.|first source:Le premier texte insiste sur le coût,^contrast:tandis que^second source:le second souligne les avantages.

340|C1|Qualified conclusion|il semblerait que + subjunctive|The conditional impersonal frame presents a conclusion cautiously; the subjunctive is appropriate in this model.|Il semblerait que cette solution soit préférable.|It would seem that this solution is preferable.|Caution in wording does not replace evidence.|qualification:Il semblerait^subordinate clause:que cette solution soit préférable.

290|B2|Restriction with ne…que|ne + finite verb + que + restricted element|Ne…que means only; it does not form an ordinary negative assertion.|Je ne prends que le train.|I only take the train.|Do not add pas unless a different meaning is intended.|subject:Je^restriction opening:ne^verb:prends^restricted element:que le train.

133|A2|Impersonal adjective and infinitive|il est + adjective + de + infinitive|Il is an impersonal placeholder when the following infinitive describes the activity.|Il est utile de vérifier.|It is useful to check.|C’est utile can introduce a different sentence structure.|impersonal frame:Il est utile^infinitive phrase:de vérifier.

137|A2|Verb-specific preposition|verb + à/de + infinitive|The governing verb determines the preposition; it cannot be copied mechanically from English.|Je commence à comprendre.|I am starting to understand.|Commencer à contrasts with essayer de.|subject:Je^governing verb:commence^infinitive phrase:à comprendre.

171|B1|Missing someone|missed person + manquer + à-person pronoun|The person being missed is the French subject.|Tu me manques.|I miss you.|Je te manque means you miss me.|subject:Tu^experiencer:me^verb:manques.

88|A2|Impersonal obligation|il faut + infinitive|Falloir is impersonal and uses il; the following action can remain an infinitive.|Il faut partir maintenant.|We have to leave now.|Do not invent je faux or nous fallons.|impersonal necessity:Il faut^infinitive:partir^time:maintenant.
